attribution.reason: The head moves CA bundle extraction and loading from cert_verify, which ran per verified request, to module import.

consequence: Importing requests extracts and loads the CA bundle even when no HTTPS request follows. An upstream report shows PermissionError raised by the import in a multi-user deployment that loads the package from a zip archive, so the importing program stops before it makes any request. Import of the adapters module takes about 4 ms longer.
exposure: Every importer pays the import cost. The import failure needs zip or pex packaging and an extracted bundle left in the temporary directory by a differently privileged user.
controls: The failure is a traceback at import. The register records no workaround, and no setting defers the load.
reversibility: No persistent effect. A downgrade or patch restores lazy loading.
workload: python -X importtime -c 'import requests': the requests.adapters module's own time rises from 2586 us to 6704 us.

grouping.reason: Both manifestations follow from the single move of the load to import time.

limits: The PermissionError was not reproduced end to end; it rests on the upstream traceback and the structural diff.
The upstream 25% import-time figure was not reproduced. The measured increase is confined to one submodule.
At the merge-base the same extraction ran on the first verified request. The newly failing operation is an import that makes no such request.
